text:
alex: Heads-up: spikes in GPU nodepool churn in us-west1 this morning. HPA fired on per-pod p95 latency and CA ended up provisioning 4 nodes, then pods scaled down and nodes stayed. We briefly hit quota and CA tried to fallback to us-east which created cross-region egress. Anyone watching?

maria: Saw the same alerts. hpa replicas 3 -> 12 in ~45s, then back to 4. CA events show scaleUp waited ~130s for nodes then added a batch. Cost spike due to idle GPUs.

sam: Is the HPA using per-pod p95? That tends to oscillate. Average-based targets are more stable for bursty request patterns.

alex: Yes, HPA is using type: Pods metric name: request_latency_p95 (custom.pods). targetValue ~200ms. stabilizationWindow is 30s currently.

ira: Metrics-adapter logs show scrape window=60s and aggregator window=60s, so we have a mismatch with HPA 30s stabilizationWindow. Bursts are getting through before CA placement completes.

devops-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout finished for inference-service v2 (build 2026-03-18-0842).

maria: CA scale-down delay is 300s, so nodes stayed long enough to cost us. Also we hit regional GPU quota in us-west1, so CA attempted provisioning in us-east1 — caused cross-region routing and latency spikes.

sam: Two angles: (1) HPA behavior + metric aggregation causing noisy scaling, (2) CA/nodepool constraints + quota fallbacks making churn expensive.

alex: Proposal: 1) switch HPA to AverageValue on a pod metric (avg latency) or move to external queue-depth metric, 2) increase HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120s, 3) align metrics-adapter scrape/window to HPA windows, 4) consider small reserved warm GPU pool or Dedicated for this service.

ira: Also consider VPA to avoid oversized requests that force fewer pods per node (VPA cannot change GPU requests but can adjust CPU/mem). KEDA could be used to scale on queue depth (Rabbit/Kafka) rather than per-pod latency so CA sees smoother load.

maria: Quick HPA snippet I want to propose in a PR:

alex: ```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: request_latency_ms
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "150"
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
```

ira: For CA, recommended knobs: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m (so we don't remove nodes between quick bursts), verify --max-node-provision-time, and keep GPU nodegroup min=1 to avoid full cold starts. Also open quota request for us-west1 GPUs.

sam: Agreed. Also set HPA behavior policies (like controlled surge) to avoid immediate doubling. If we move to queue-depth external metric, CA will see steady pod count growth instead of jitter.

maria: I'll open the runbook + PR: (1) change HPA to AverageValue + stabilizationWindow, (2) align metrics-adapter windows, (3) create a 1-node warm GPU nodepool or request Dedicated capacity, (4) submit quota request to GCE for us-west1 GPUs.

alex: :thumbsup: Thanks. Let's monitor 2 hours after merge and watch cost and node churn dashboards. If spike repeats, we'll fall back to scheduled warm pool.

ira: I'll also add a Canary in us-west1 with KEDA scaled by queue depth to test the external-metric approach in prod-lite.

sam: FYI for future: prefer average-based pod metrics for HPA when CA-backed node provisioning latency is >60s.

maria: Opening PR and runbook now.

alex: Thanks all.
